description: A .NET 10 extension-based CLI framework (the `az` binary) for Azure resource management, with an out-of-process AI agent fallback built on the GitHub Copilot SDK, a full-screen interactive Terminal UI (Hex1b), and mirrored PowerShell cmdlets. The product/code identity is 'Azclips' (namespaces, binaries, ~/.azclips state) even though the GitHub repository itself is named 'cirrus' (`git remote -v` -> github.com/Azure/cirrus.git) — the two names refer to the same codebase and should not be conflated as separate projects.

generatedAgainst.note: This refresh corrects several stale claims found in README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/spec/ARCHITECTURE.md and the previous wiki/catalogue.json: (1) the AI fallback is NOT the TUI — the CLI's Program.TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:318) spawns a SEPARATE standalone process, azclips-agent.exe (Agent/Core.Agent.csproj, AssemblyName 'azclips-agent'), independent of Core.Tui; (2) the agent is built on the GitHub Copilot SDK (GitHub.Copilot.SDK 1.0.0, Agent/Core.Agent.csproj:49) driving a bundled 'copilot' daemon over stdio (Agent/BundledDaemonResolver.cs), NOT Azure OpenAI directly, though the built-in provider still authenticates via Azure/MSAL (Agent/Providers/BuiltinProviderConfig.cs); (3) AgentModeEntry (the chat-loop host) lives under Agent/AgentMode/, having moved out of Core.Tui; (4) src/PS now has six module folders (Az, Common, Compute, Config, Login, Resources) plus TelemetryHelper.ps1, not just Login/Resources as README.md's Quick Start still shows; (5) src/Extensions now includes a Compute extension (VM commands) alongside Config, Extension, ExtensionRuntime, Login, Resources; (6) Agent tool implementations live under Agent/Tools/{Env,Help,Resource/Cache,Resource/Sku,Shell} and are also exposed as first-class `az agent tool ...` CLI commands via a dedicated extension, Agent/Commands (Agent.Commands.csproj) — not folded into ChatAgent.cs.

modules.title: Getting Started
modules.summary: Orientation for new users and contributors: what Azclips is, how it is built, and how to drive its four client surfaces — the `az` CLI, PowerShell modules, the interactive Terminal UI, and the opt-in AI agent fallback.

children.title: Overview & Architecture
children.prompt: Explain what Project Azclips is and give the 10,000-foot architecture, grounded in real code, not README.md's stale narrative. Note up front that the GitHub repository is Azure/cirrus but every namespace, binary name, and on-disk state directory uses the 'Azclips'/'azclips' identity (Shared.props:3 <Product>Azclips</Product>, ~/.azclips via src/Core/Core.Abstractions/HomePaths.cs:10-12) — these are the same codebase, not two products. Cover the four client surfaces that all share one DI composition root: CLI (src/CLI/Program.cs), PowerShell cmdlets (src/PS/), an interactive Terminal UI (TUI/Program.cs, Core.Tui.csproj), and a standalone AI agent process (Agent/Core.Agent.csproj, AssemblyName 'azclips-agent'). Trace the CLI happy path: Program.Main (src/CLI/Program.cs:38) -> AzclipsServiceProvider.Initialize(ClientType.CLI) (src/Core/Core.DependencyInjection/AzclipsServiceProvider.cs:67) -> the extension dispatcher -> IEngine.OpenExecutionSession (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IEngine.cs:8, implemented at src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:39) -> ExecutionSession.RunAsync (src/Core/Core.Engine/ExecutionSession.cs:57). Then the failure path: on HttpRequestException or any unhandled exception, Program.TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:318) spawns azclips-agent.exe as a CHILD PROCESS with inherited stdio (ProcessStartInfo at src/CLI/Program.cs:369-387) — this is the critical correction versus older docs claiming the TUI hosts the fallback. Call out target framework net10.0 (global.json:3, src/Directory.Build.props:4) and the AgentOptions.Enabled opt-in gate (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/AgentOptions.cs:11), off by default for private preview. Include a system-context Mermaid diagram (dark-mode colors) showing CLI, PowerShell, TUI, and the agent process around the shared Engine/DI core.

children.title: Environment Setup
children.prompt: Step-by-step environment setup grounded in the actual solution layout. Prerequisites: .NET 10 SDK pinned to exactly 10.0.203 with rollForward latestMinor (global.json:1-6), PowerShell 7+ for the PS modules, and Microsoft.PowerShell.PlatyPS only for help-artifact generation via build/Install-BuildDependencies.ps1. Walk the solution file azclips.slnx: src/CLI (Core.Cli), 9+ Core.* libraries under src/Core/ (Abstractions, ArgumentParsing, AssemblyLoading, Authentication, Configuration, DependencyInjection, Engine, Extensions, Runtime, Telemetry), 6 extension projects under src/Extensions/ (Compute, Config, Extension, ExtensionRuntime, Login, Resources), TUI (Core.Tui), Agent (Core.Agent + Agent.Commands + Core.Agent.Tools), src/PS/{Az,Common,Compute,Config,Login,Resources}, tests/, and tools/Help. Show `dotnet build -c Release azclips.slnx` producing artifacts under artifacts/Release/<ExtName>/ per the OutputPath convention in Shared.props:9 (OutputPath=$(RepoArtifacts)$(Configuration)/$(ExtName)/) and src/Directory.Build.props (net10.0, Nullable, TreatWarningsAsErrors:10). Cover build/build.ps1 and build/Set-ModuleConfiguration.ps1 for staging PowerShell modules. Show where user state lands: ~/.azclips (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/HomePaths.cs:12 DefaultHomeDirectoryName) for config/registry/trace/arm-cache, and {LocalApplicationData}/.azclips for the auth context file (HomePaths.cs:56-57). Verify with `dotnet --info` matching global.json.

children.title: CLI Usage
children.prompt: Practical guide to the `az` CLI as it exists today. Show structured extension commands (`az group create ...`, `az vm ...` from the Compute extension, `az config set/get/list/delete/info`, `az login`, `az extension add/list`) using the help docs under src/CLI/Help/Docs/ as the authoritative surface. Explain global flag parsing in Program.cs: ParseDebugFlag / --debug (src/CLI/Program.cs:192), ParseOutputFlag / --output json|plain (src/CLI/Program.cs:257), ParseNoCacheFlag / --no-cache setting AZCLIPS_NO_EXTENSION_CACHE (src/CLI/Program.cs:283). Trace the error-handling ladder in Main's try/catch (around src/CLI/Program.cs:140-181): AzclipsErrorException renders structured JSON/text with no AI fallback (src/CLI/Program.cs:165-172), while HttpRequestException and any other unhandled Exception both call TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:163, :180). Explain the fallback UX from TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:318): the agent.enabled config gate, the non-interactive/redirected-stdio guard for interactive sessionStyle (src/CLI/Program.cs:347-351), and the AZCLIPS_IN_AGENT_MODE recursion guard (src/CLI/Program.cs:26, :355-358). Include a Mermaid sequence diagram (autonumber) of parse -> execute -> structured-error-or-fallback.

children.title: PowerShell Module Usage
children.prompt: Guide to the PowerShell surface. The cmdlet/module projects live under src/PS/{Az,Common,Compute,Config,Login,Resources} (see azclips.slnx) with manifests such as src/PS/Compute/Compute.psd1 and src/PS/Login/Login.psd1. Show importing modules and using cmdlets (e.g. Connect-AzAccount, New-AzVM / Get-AzVM / Remove-AzVM from src/PS/Compute/Cmdlets/NewVMCmdlet.cs, GetVMCmdlet.cs, RemoveVMCmdlet.cs, and Set-AzConfig for config/telemetry opt-out). Explain how cmdlets share the SAME engine as the CLI: they call AzclipsServiceProvider.Initialize(ClientType.PowerShell) (src/Core/Core.DependencyInjection/AzclipsServiceProvider.cs:67) and resolve IEngine, then open an execution session whose output is pumped through a per-invocation channel back to $PSCmdlet.WriteObject via CmdletOutputStreamsFactory (src/PS/Common/CmdletOutputStreamsFactory.cs:28). Note the .psd1 manifests and any help markdown under each src/PS/<Module>/help/, and TelemetryHelper.ps1 (src/PS/TelemetryHelper.ps1) used by module-level telemetry opt-out. Include a Mermaid diagram showing Cmdlet -> AzclipsServiceProvider -> Engine -> output channel -> WriteObject.

children.title: Terminal UI Quickstart
children.prompt: Introduce the interactive Terminal UI (Core.Tui.csproj) as a distinct client surface from the CLI. Show launching it (the built binary from artifacts, or `dotnet run` against TUI/Core.Tui.csproj) and its full-screen Hex1b-based shell built in TUI/Program.cs:20 (Main) and TUI/Program.cs:77 (BuildUI). Explain the two shell modes toggled by F2 or `/mode` — ShellMode.Azure (default, runs `az` under the hood) and ShellMode.Local (runs the system shell) — defined in TUI/Models.cs:6 and toggled by AppState.ToggleMode (TUI/AppState.cs:173) via TUI/commands/ModeCommand.cs:6. Walk a first session: typing a command calls AppState.ExecuteCommand (TUI/AppState.cs:254), which for Azure mode shells out to the `az` binary through ProcessService.RunCliAsync (TUI/services/ProcessService.cs:27) and streams stdout/stderr into the scrollable history panel (TUI/Rendering/HistoryRenderer.cs). Cover slash commands (/cd, /ls, /pwd, /mode, /refresh, /copy, /exit under TUI/commands/) and key bindings (F1 help, Ctrl+L clear, Ctrl+C cancel) wired in TUI/Program.cs's InputBindings block. Mention that the Azure VFS (`/cd`, `/ls`) browses real Azure resources via TUI/Azure/AzureVfs.cs and TUI/Azure/ArmClient.cs. Include a short Mermaid flow of keypress -> AppState -> ProcessService/AzureVfs -> history render.

children.title: AI Agent Fallback Quickstart
children.prompt: Practical guide to opting into and using the AI agent fallback. Show enabling it: `az config set --key agent.enabled --value true` (gate read in src/Core/Core.Abstractions/AgentOptions.cs:11, checked in src/CLI/Program.cs:324-338). Explain the two session styles from AgentOptions.SessionStyle (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/AgentOptions.cs:17): 'oneshot' (default — proposes a fix and exits, safe even with redirected stdio) versus 'interactive' (a chat loop gated behind a live-TTY check at src/CLI/Program.cs:347-351). Walk a real failure: an `az` command throws, TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:318) spawns azclips-agent.exe with --agent-mode --failed-command ... --error ... (src/CLI/Program.cs:396-403), which AgentModeEntry.RunAsync (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:24) picks up: it prints a banner (or stays quiet in oneshot), builds a ChatAgent (Agent/ChatAgent.cs:102 CreateAsync), and runs a turn loop that proposes a plan the user must approve before any command executes. Cover the interaction brake (soft reminder at 12 exchanges, hard stop at 20 — Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:21-22) and Ctrl+C/abort semantics (Agent/Hosting/AbortKeyWatcher.cs). Include a Mermaid sequence diagram (autonumber): failed command -> agent spawn -> propose_plan -> user approval -> submit_response.

modules.title: Deep Dive
modules.summary: Architecture-level explanations grouped by concern. Every leaf traces real code paths with file:line citations and calls out where prior documentation drifted from the current source. Organized into three groups so no section exceeds eight children.

children.title: Agent, Copilot SDK & Interactive Surfaces
children.summary: The out-of-process AI agent (GitHub Copilot SDK), its tools/prompts/plan protocol, the dual rendering systems, and how the Terminal UI relates to and hosts agent behavior.

children.title: Agent Architecture
children.prompt: Deep dive on the standalone agent process (Agent/ -> Core.Agent.csproj, AssemblyName azclips-agent, OutputType Exe per Agent/Core.Agent.csproj:5-6). Trace the full lifecycle: Program.Main (Agent/Program.cs:9) dispatches only on `--agent-mode` to AgentModeEntry.RunAsync (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:24), which initializes its OWN DI container as ClientType.CLI (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:36 — a deliberate choice documented in-code: 'was TUI back when this entry lived inside Core.Tui'), resolves IAuthService/IProfileService/IConfigurationService, reads AgentOptions (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:44), and picks the prompt/quiet mode based on IsInteractive (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:47-50). Explain SessionState (Agent/SessionState.cs:11) as the per-session mutable gate shared with the PreToolUse hook — PlanApproved, IsOneShot, SubmittedThisTurn — and how ChatAgent (Agent/ChatAgent.cs:27) tracks _sendCalledClosingTool (Agent/ChatAgent.cs:43, LastSendCalledClosingTool:52) to enforce the 'always act through tools' contract, retried up to MaxToolEnforcementRetries=3 in AgentModeEntry.SendWithToolEnforcementAsync (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:226). Cover the escape valve (soft 12 / hard 20 exchanges, Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:21-22) and the RunChatLoopAsync (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:136) split between one-shot drain and interactive `> ` prompt loop. Trace how it is invoked: CLI's TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:318) child-process spawn with inherited stdio. Diagrams: process/lifecycle sequence (autonumber) and a state diagram of SessionState's plan/submit gates.

children.title: Copilot SDK Integration
children.prompt: Explain exactly how azclips integrates the GitHub Copilot SDK (GitHub.Copilot.SDK 1.0.0, Agent/Core.Agent.csproj:49). Trace ChatAgent.CreateAsync (Agent/ChatAgent.cs:102): it builds a CopilotClient with RuntimeConnection.ForStdio pointed at a bundled daemon resolved by BundledDaemonResolver.Resolve (Agent/BundledDaemonResolver.cs:13), which locates the platform-specific 'copilot'/'copilot.exe' binary under a runtimes/<rid>/native/ layout whose base path is decided by AgentInstallLayout (Agent/AgentInstallLayout.cs:22) — packaged builds read Extensions/Microsoft.Azure.Azclips.Extensions.Agent/deps/runtimes/<rid>/native/, dev builds read NuGet's default runtimes/<rid>/native/ next to the exe, distinguished at compile time by the AGENT_DEV_BUILD constant (Agent/Core.Agent.csproj:22, Agent/AgentInstallLayout.cs:24-28). Cover provider construction: BuiltinProviderConfig.BuildAsync (Agent/Providers/BuiltinProviderConfig.cs:16) acquires an ARM-scoped MSAL token via IAuthService.AcquireTokenSilentlyAsync and builds an Azure-type ProviderConfig pointing at the APIM-fronted GPT endpoint (BuiltinProviderOptions defaults in src/Core/Core.Abstractions/AgentOptions.cs:54-59). Explain the SDK's hook surface wired by ChatAgent — OnPreToolUse -> PreToolUseHook.HandleAsync (Agent/Hooks/PreToolUseHook.cs:19) — and how EventRenderer.Forward (Agent/EventRenderer.cs:36) translates GitHub.Copilot SessionEvent types (AssistantMessageDeltaEvent, ToolExecutionStartEvent/CompleteEvent, AssistantUsageEvent, SessionErrorEvent) into azclips's host-agnostic AgentEvent hierarchy (Agent/AgentEvents.cs:18). Diagram: component diagram of CopilotClient/CopilotSession/BundledDaemonResolver/ProviderConfig plus a sequence for one turn's SDK event stream.

children.title: Agent Tools
children.prompt: Catalog and trace every tool the agent can call, split across two projects. (1) Core.Agent.Tools (Agent/Tools/Core.Agent.Tools.csproj), consumed by both the agent exe and the CLI extension: EnvironmentProber.ProbeAsync (Agent/Tools/Env/EnvironmentProber.cs:19) builds an EnvironmentSnapshot (OS, shell, cwd forwarded via AZCLIPS_CALLER_CWD); HelpTools (Agent/Tools/Help/HelpTools.cs:19) exposes list_commands/get_command by shelling out to `az agent tool help`; the Resource/Cache subtree (Agent/Tools/Resource/Cache/: ResourceCache.cs, CachedResourceTools.cs, ArmCacheRefresher.cs, ArmDetailsClient.cs, AuthServiceTokenCredential.cs, FileLockHelper.cs) backs find/show/tree resource lookups against a local ARM cache; Resource/Sku/AvailableLocationsTool.cs checks VM SKU/region availability; Shell/ShellOutHelper.cs wraps process execution for the help/resource tools. (2) The turn-closing tools live in Agent/Hosting/ as Microsoft.Extensions.AI AIFunctions: ProposePlanTool (Agent/Hosting/ProposePlanTool.cs:21, AIFunctionFactory.Create at :25) and SubmitResponseTool (Agent/Hosting/SubmitResponseTool.cs:20) — both bodies only log via ToolInvocationLog; real validation/rendering happens in the PreToolUseHook. (3) The SAME internal tools are re-exposed as first-class `az agent tool ...` CLI commands via a separate extension, Agent.Commands (Agent/Commands/ExtensionIndex.cs:11, [ExtensionVerb("agent")]), with processors under Agent/Commands/Processors/ (EnvProcessor.cs, HelpProcessor.cs, Resource/ResourceFindProcessor.cs, ResourceSkuProcessor.cs, ResourceTreeProcessor.cs, ResourceShowProcessor.cs, ResourceRefreshProcessor.cs) — so external programs (Copilot CLI, Claude Code Skills) can invoke them without a full chat loop. Diagram: tool taxonomy (env / help / resource-cache / sku / shell / plan-protocol) and which project owns each.

children.title: Prompts & Plan Mode
children.prompt: Explain the system prompts and the propose_plan / submit_response protocol that gives the agent human-in-the-loop safety. The two prompt files, Agent/prompts/inline.md and Agent/prompts/oneshot.md, are selected by AgentModeEntry based on AgentOptions.IsInteractive (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:47) and copied to the output dir via the csproj's `<None Update="prompts\*.md">` item (Agent/Core.Agent.csproj:72-77). Trace FailedCommandHelp.BuildContextAsync (Agent/Plan/FailedCommandHelp.cs:21): it conservatively extracts a command verb from the failed input (ExtractCommandName, Agent/Plan/FailedCommandHelp.cs:84) and pre-fetches its help text via the same path get_command uses, injecting it into session start context so the agent doesn't spend a turn re-discovering the command it was triggered by. Trace PlanArgsParser (Agent/Plan/PlanArgsParser.cs:12): ValidateSubmitResponse (:20) enforces the completed/rejected/failed status enum and the OUT_OF_SCOPE_ message convention; ValidateProposePlan (:42) requires non-empty issues and steps with label+cmd; HasDangerVerb (:172) auto-flags delete/remove/purge/... commands as destructive even if the model didn't say so. Trace the enforcement point, PreToolUseHook.HandleAsync (Agent/Hooks/PreToolUseHook.cs:19): the post-terminator gate denying tool calls after submit_response (:30), the submit_response branch that renders the final outcome and sets SubmitRendered/SubmittedThisTurn (:42-82), the propose_plan branch gating bash/powershell behind PlanApproved (:89-171), and PlaceholderDetector.TryDetect (Agent/Hooks/PlaceholderDetector.cs:16) denying commands containing unfilled <placeholder>/{{...}}/YOUR_*/*-PLACEHOLDER tokens. Diagram: a state machine for propose_plan -> approval -> execute -> submit_response, plus the prompt-selection branch.

children.title: Rendering & Terminal UX
children.prompt: Explain azclips's TWO distinct rendering systems and why they differ. (1) Agent console rendering (Agent/Hosting/): IAgentRenderer (Agent/Hosting/IAgentRenderer.cs) is implemented by ConsoleAgentRenderer (Agent/Hosting/ConsoleAgentRenderer.cs:7), which prints plain-line output for the agent's chat loop (streaming tokens, tool start/complete/fail, plan/approval prompts via ConsoleApprovalPrompt) and suppresses trailing model prose once submit_response has rendered (SetOnFinalRendered wiring, Agent/ChatAgent.cs and Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:108). TraceAgentRenderer (Agent/Hosting/TraceAgentRenderer.cs:15) decorates it to additionally append a JSONL trace file when agent.trace.enabled (path expansion for a leading '~' at Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:355-362). SpinnerService (Agent/Hosting/SpinnerService.cs) shows a busy indicator while a turn is in flight, raced against ConsoleApprovalPrompt.PumpOneAsync so an approval prompt can interrupt it (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:260-330 SendAndPumpAsync); AbortKeyWatcher (Agent/Hosting/AbortKeyWatcher.cs) owns Ctrl+C during a turn. RendererLoggingService (Agent/Hosting/RendererLoggingService.cs) funnels azclips's own Warn/Error logs through the renderer's lock instead of racing stdout directly. (2) TUI full-screen rendering (TUI/Rendering/): built on the Hex1b widget library — HeaderRenderer, FooterRenderer, HistoryRenderer, MenuBarRenderer, SuggestionRenderer, HelpRenderer compose the VStack/HStack widget tree assembled in TUI/Program.cs:87 BuildUI, themed via TuiTheme.Load/CreateBaseTheme (TUI/Rendering/TuiTheme.cs) and raw ANSI helpers in TUI/Rendering/Ansi.cs. Contrast the two: the agent renderer is a simple append-only console stream meant to be readable when spawned as a child process with inherited stdio, while the TUI renderer owns the whole terminal buffer and repaints via Hex1b's diffing engine. Diagram: two parallel rendering pipelines (agent turn events -> IAgentRenderer chain; TUI AppState -> Hex1b widget tree).

children.title: TUI Agent Mode & Fallback Interplay
children.prompt: Explain precisely how the Terminal UI relates to the AI agent fallback — a subtle seam worth its own page because the TUI does NOT host a chat mode itself; it runs `az` as a redirected child process, which changes how the CLI's own fallback behaves. Trace ProcessService.RunCliAsync (TUI/services/ProcessService.cs:27): it launches the `az` binary with RedirectStandardOutput=true and RedirectStandardError=true (TUI/services/ProcessService.cs:41-42) but does not redirect stdin, and critically this makes Console.IsOutputRedirected true inside that child `az` process. Trace the consequence in TryAgentFallbackAsync's interactive guard (src/CLI/Program.cs:347-351): `if (agentOptions.IsInteractive && (Console.IsInputRedirected || Console.IsOutputRedirected)) return 1;` — so when a command run from inside the TUI fails, INTERACTIVE agent sessionStyle is silently disabled, while ONESHOT sessionStyle still works because it is not gated (src/CLI/Program.cs:340-351 comment explains the rationale) and inherits stdio (RedirectStandardInput=false at src/CLI/Program.cs:386) so streaming/plan output still reaches the TUI's captured stdout stream and is classified into HistoryItemType.Output/Error lines (TUI/services/ProcessService.cs:179-186 ClassifyLine). Cover ShellMode (TUI/Models.cs:6 — Azure vs Local) and how AppState.ExecuteCommand (TUI/AppState.cs:254) branches: Local mode never touches `az` or the agent at all (plain shell via ProcessService.RunLocalAsync); Azure mode always goes through `az`, so agent fallback (oneshot only) is reachable from the TUI in that mode. Cover the AZCLIPS_IN_AGENT_MODE recursion guard (src/CLI/Program.cs:26) that would prevent a nested spawn if the TUI itself were ever launched from inside an agent session. Diagram: sequence showing TUI -> ProcessService.RunCliAsync -> az (child) -> TryAgentFallbackAsync -> azclips-agent.exe (grandchild) -> streamed output back through the TUI's redirected pipes into HistoryRenderer.

children.title: TUI Interactive Shell & Azure VFS
children.prompt: Deep dive on the non-agent half of the Terminal UI: its Azure Virtual File System and shell ergonomics. Trace TUI/Program.cs:22-40, which PrependRegistration's ArmClient, AzureVfs, ProcessService, PromptService, HistoryService, AppState and OverrideRegistration's a silent TuiLoggingService plus TUITelemetryProvider before calling AzclipsServiceProvider.Initialize(ClientType.TUI) (TUI/Program.cs:40) — showing how the TUI customizes the shared DI container rather than forking the engine. Cover AzureVfs (TUI/Azure/AzureVfs.cs) and ArmClient (TUI/Azure/ArmClient.cs) which present subscriptions/resource groups/resources as a navigable path (`/sub/rg/resource`) driving `/cd` and `/ls` (TUI/commands/CdCommand.cs, LsCommand.cs). Trace AppState (TUI/AppState.cs:14) as the coordinator: EditorState-backed InputText/CursorPos (:29-39), thread-safe History via a lock (:60-81), UpdateSuggestions delegating to CompletionService (:195-211, TUI/services/CompletionService.cs), and ExecuteCommand's slash-command dispatch (:254-307) via the ISlashCommand registry (TUI/commands/ISlashCommand.cs) covering Cd/Ls/Pwd/Mode/Refresh/Copy/Exit. Cover CustomShellWorkload / AzclipsShellWorkload (TUI/services/AzclipsShellWorkload.cs:13) which hand-rolls ANSI cursor movement and raw-byte input parsing (arrow keys, Ctrl+A/E/K/U/W, UTF-8 multi-byte decode) for the prompt line, and HistoryService (TUI/services/HistoryService.cs) for per-mode command history navigation. Diagram: AppState-centric component diagram linking Vfs, ProcessService, CompletionService, HistoryService and the slash-command registry.

children.title: Core Runtime, Auth & Extensibility
children.summary: The composition root and engine every client shares, the HTTP execution pipeline, MSAL-based authentication, the extension model, and the PowerShell cmdlet architecture built on top of the same engine.

children.title: Core Engine & Orchestration
children.prompt: The single most important architectural page. Trace the composition-root + session model every client (CLI, PowerShell, TUI, Agent) flows through. (1) DI bootstrap: AzclipsServiceProvider (src/Core/Core.DependencyInjection/AzclipsServiceProvider.cs:17) with PrependRegistration/OverrideRegistration (:29, :44) letting each client customize the container BEFORE RegisterAzclipsServices chains every module's DIRegisterExtensions (:53), then idempotent Initialize(ClientType) (:67). Show each client's customization point: CLI (src/CLI/Program.cs:57-60 PrependRegistration), TUI (TUI/Program.cs:22-38), Agent (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:36 — Initialize(ClientType.CLI), not a distinct Agent client type). (2) The Engine: a partial mediator class (src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:22) implementing IEngine (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IEngine.cs:8); OpenExecutionSession (:39) caches extension indices via LFUCache<Lazy<IExtensionIndex>> (:36), and CreateProcessorContext (:99) resolves the active Profile (ResolveProfileAsync, :151) and builds the HTTP pipeline with the auth handler prepended. (3) ExecutionSession (src/Core/Core.Engine/ExecutionSession.cs:12): channel-based isolated output, RunAsync (:57) driving the resolved IProcessor. (4) Orchestration/fallback: Program.Main's try/catch (src/CLI/Program.cs:140-181) distinguishes structured AzclipsErrorException (no fallback) from HttpRequestException/generic Exception, both routing to TryAgentFallbackAsync (src/CLI/Program.cs:318) which spawns the SEPARATE azclips-agent.exe process — NOT an in-process OrchestratorEngine/AgentEngine as some historical docs describe. Diagrams: component diagram of the DI graph, and a sequence diagram (autonumber) of a full invocation with fallback.

children.title: HTTP Pipeline & Runtime
children.prompt: Explain the runtime HTTP execution layer in Core.Runtime. Trace HttpPipeline (src/Core/Core.Runtime/HttpPipeline.cs:15, implementing IRuntimeHttpPipeline) and HttpPipelineService (src/Core/Core.Runtime/HttpPipelineService.cs), which compose delegating handlers around HttpClientFactory-produced clients. Trace how Engine.CreateProcessorContext (src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:99) prepends an auth handler backed by the resolved Profile/IAuthService before any extension's IProcessor runs. Cover SendAsyncFactory and SendAsyncTerminalFactory (src/Core/Core.Runtime/SendAsyncFactory.cs, SendAsyncTerminalFactory.cs) as the seams used to swap in mocked terminal senders for tests. Cover RuntimeEventBus (src/Core/Core.Runtime/RuntimeEventBus.cs) for cross-cutting runtime event publication, and ConsoleOutputAdapter / ConsoleLoggingService / ScopedLoggingService (src/Core/Core.Runtime/) for output and log routing — noting that ScopedLoggingService.UseScope is exactly what the agent process swaps out for RendererLoggingService (Agent/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs:90) so azclips-internal logs don't race the spinner. Cover the IProcessor/ProcessorContext contract every extension command implements, and CommandLoadingExtension (src/Core/Core.Runtime/CommandLoadingExtension.cs). Diagram: the delegating-handler chain (auth -> pipeline -> real send) as a Mermaid flow, contrasted with the test-time terminal-factory substitution.

children.title: Authentication (MSAL)
children.prompt: Explain the authentication subsystem. MsalAuthService (src/Core/Core.Authentication/MsalAuthService.cs:10) implements IAuthService (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IAuthService.cs) using Microsoft.Identity.Client: LoginAsync (:19) branches between interactive and device-code flows, LogoutAsync(userPrincipalName) (:30) removes only the matching account from the MSAL token cache, AcquireTokenSilentlyAsync (:135) is what both the engine's auth handler and the agent's BuiltinProviderConfig (Agent/Providers/BuiltinProviderConfig.cs:24) call to get a token without prompting, and CanAcquireTokenSilentlyAsync (:178) probes cache validity. Cover AzureCredentialFactory (src/Core/Core.Authentication/AzureCredentialFactory.cs) for building Azure.Core TokenCredential instances, ManagedIdentityAuthenticator (src/Core/Core.Authentication/ManagedIdentity/) for MI scenarios, SubscriptionService (src/Core/Core.Authentication/SubscriptionService.cs) for subscription/tenant resolution, and AuthConstants/AuthResultExtensions (src/Core/Core.Authentication/AuthConstants.cs, AuthResultExtensions.cs). Explain how the resolved Profile (not a standalone AuthContext/context.json) is the source of truth flowing through ProcessorContext, and how AZCLIPS_CALLER_CWD / the agent's own auth calls reuse the exact same IAuthService rather than a parallel credential path. Diagram: sequence (autonumber) of `az login` -> MSAL interactive/device-code -> token cache -> profile activation -> silent reuse by both CLI commands and the agent's builtin provider.

children.title: Extension System
children.prompt: Explain the extension architecture end-to-end. (1) Anatomy of an extension: IExtensionIndex (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IExtensionIndex.cs) implemented per extension (e.g. src/Extensions/Compute/ExtensionIndex.cs, src/Extensions/Login/ExtensionIndex.cs, src/Extensions/Config/ExtensionIndex.cs, Agent/Commands/ExtensionIndex.cs:11), each mapping CLI/PowerShell command names to IProcessor implementations (see src/Extensions/Compute/Processors/, src/Extensions/Config/Commands/{GetConfigCommand.cs,SetConfigCommand.cs,ListConfigCommand.cs,DeleteConfigCommand.cs,InfoConfigCommand.cs} sharing ConfigCommandBase). (2) Registration & resolution: ExtensionRegistry / ExtensionRegistryEntry (src/Core/Core.Extensions/ExtensionRegistry.cs:20, :67), FileExtensionRegistryStore (src/Core/Core.Extensions/FileExtensionRegistryStore.cs) persisting to the registry.json under ~/.azclips/extensions (HomePaths.cs:13-14, :32-33), ExtensionResolver and ExtensionCandidateSelector (src/Core/Core.Extensions/ExtensionResolver.cs, ExtensionCandidateSelector.cs) picking among installed versions, CompatibilityGuard (src/Core/Core.Extensions/CompatibilityGuard.cs) enforcing per-extension Compatibility.cs declarations (e.g. src/Extensions/Compute/Compatibility.cs). (3) Built-ins vs installable: BuiltInExtensions (src/Core/Core.Extensions/BuiltInExtensions.cs) versus the Extension management extension (`az extension add/list/remove`, src/Extensions/Extension/) with ExtensionAddPlanner (src/Core/Core.Extensions/ExtensionAddPlanner.cs). (4) Metadata plumbing: LeafIndex/LeafReader/RegistryLookup/ExtensionVerbReader (src/Core/Core.Extensions/) and ExtensionMetadataContext. (5) ExtensionRuntime (src/Extensions/ExtensionRuntime/) — the JSON serialization/type-conversion layer extensions use to (de)serialize ARM payloads. Diagram: extension resolution/loading sequence (autonumber) from CLI verb to loaded IProcessor.

children.title: PowerShell Cmdlet Architecture
children.prompt: Explain how the PowerShell surface is built on the SAME engine as the CLI rather than a parallel implementation. Trace a cmdlet like NewVMCmdlet (src/PS/Compute/Cmdlets/NewVMCmdlet.cs) or GetVMCmdlet.cs / RemoveVMCmdlet.cs: each cmdlet's ProcessRecord calls AzclipsServiceProvider.Initialize(ClientType.PowerShell) (src/Core/Core.DependencyInjection/AzclipsServiceProvider.cs:67), resolves IEngine, and opens an ExecutionSession exactly as the CLI does (link to Core Engine & Orchestration). Trace CmdletOutputStreamsFactory (src/PS/Common/CmdletOutputStreamsFactory.cs:28) — the internal static class that builds OutputStreams delegates routing WriteOutput/WriteError/WriteVerbose back to $PSCmdlet.WriteObject/WriteError/WriteVerbose so the engine's channel-based output model works identically for a blocking cmdlet call as it does for a long-running CLI process. Cover the module layout: six module projects under src/PS/ (Az, Common, Compute, Config, Login, Resources) each with a .psd1 manifest (e.g. src/PS/Compute/Compute.psd1, src/PS/Login/Login.psd1) and, for script modules, exported functions; TelemetryHelper.ps1 (src/PS/TelemetryHelper.ps1) shared across modules for telemetry opt-out. Note that Login is a binary module requiring `dotnet build` first, while script modules like Resources work directly from source. Diagram: Cmdlet.ProcessRecord -> AzclipsServiceProvider -> IEngine -> ExecutionSession -> CmdletOutputStreamsFactory -> WriteObject.

children.title: Platform: Configuration, Telemetry, Packaging & Quality
children.summary: Cross-cutting platform concerns: typed configuration, privacy-respecting telemetry, the multi-flavor packaging/install pipeline, and the test/build toolchain.

children.title: Configuration Management
children.prompt: Explain the configuration subsystem end-to-end. ConfigurationService (src/Core/Core.Configuration/Implementation/ConfigurationService.cs:14) implements IConfigurationService (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IConfigurationService.cs), reading/writing through FileConfigurationProvider (src/Core/Core.Configuration/Implementation/FileConfigurationProvider.cs) which persists to ~/.azclips/config.json (HomePaths.cs:15, :35-36) and validating unknown/typed keys via DefaultConfigurationValidator (src/Core/Core.Configuration/Implementation/DefaultConfigurationValidator.cs) against ConfigurationSchema (src/Core/Core.Configuration/Schema/ConfigurationSchema.cs). Trace GetConfiguration<T>() binding raw JSON into strongly-typed options: AgentOptions (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/AgentOptions.cs:6 — Enabled, Provider, SessionStyle, Interactive.Verbose, Trace.Enabled/Path, Builtin.{Endpoint,Scope,ModelId,ApiVersion}), TelemetryOptions (src/Core/Core.Abstractions/TelemetryOptions.cs), and the Core.Configuration/Options/ set (AssemblyLoadingOptions.cs, ClientsOptions.cs, DefaultsOptions.cs, ExtensionsOptions.cs). Trace the `az config` extension surface: ConfigCommandBase (src/Extensions/Config/Commands/ConfigCommandBase.cs) shared by GetConfigCommand.cs, SetConfigCommand.cs, ListConfigCommand.cs, DeleteConfigCommand.cs, InfoConfigCommand.cs, including key normalization (dot/colon notation) and the `--force` escape hatch for unknown keys. Reference docs/howto/config.md and docs/spec/config-implementation.md for the documented key catalog, and cross-check it against ConfigurationSchema.cs for drift. Diagram: `az config set` -> ConfigCommandBase -> ConfigurationService -> FileConfigurationProvider -> config.json, and a second arrow showing GetConfiguration<AgentOptions>() consumed by TryAgentFallbackAsync.

children.title: Telemetry & Observability
children.prompt: Explain the telemetry subsystem (Core.Telemetry). TelemetryService (src/Core/Core.Telemetry/TelemetryService.cs:13) implements ITelemetryService and starts root/per-command Activities via a System.Diagnostics ActivitySource, tagged through TelemetryPropertyResolver and TelemetryTags. Cover the privacy model: DefaultTelemetryPropertyFilter / DefaultTelemetryActivityNameFilter and their *Processor variants (src/Core/Core.Telemetry/DefaultTelemetryPropertyFilter.cs, DefaultTelemetryPropertyFilterProcessor.cs, DefaultTelemetryActivityNameFilter.cs, DefaultActivityNameFilterProcessor.cs) strip parameter VALUES/URLs, keeping only parameter names + success/failure + basic environment data — matching the privacy claim in README.md's Telemetry section. Cover the async export path: FileExporter/FileTelemetrySender (src/Core/Core.Telemetry/FileExporter.cs, FileTelemetrySender.cs) buffer traces to disk, then a background `--upload-telemetry` invocation (src/CLI/Program.cs:43-47) reads pending traces via DirectTelemetrySender against WellKnownEndpoints (src/Core/Core.Telemetry/DirectTelemetrySender.cs, WellKnownEndpoints.cs). Cover per-client ITelemetryProvider implementations: DefaultTelemetryProvider (src/Core/Core.Telemetry/DefaultTelemetryProvider.cs) versus TUITelemetryProvider (TUI/Telemetry/TUITelemetryProvider.cs:13), which is registered via AzclipsServiceProvider.OverrideRegistration in TUI/Program.cs:31-38 and gates entirely on TelemetryOptions.Enabled before wiring OpenTelemetry's TracerProviderBuilder (TUI/Telemetry/TUITelemetryProvider.cs:17-22). Cover the opt-out: `az config set --key telemetry.enabled --value false` / `Set-AzConfig`, and TimingActivityListener (src/Core/Core.Telemetry/TimingActivityListener.cs). Diagram: activity capture -> file buffer -> background uploader sequence (autonumber), annotated with the two ITelemetryProvider implementations.

children.title: Packaging & Distribution
children.prompt: Explain how azclips is built, signed, and shipped as installable artifacts. Trace the shared build shape: Shared.props (Product=Azclips :3, OutputPath=$(RepoArtifacts)$(Configuration)/$(ExtName)/ :9, delay-signing with MSSharedLibKey.snk in Release :18-27). Cover the two-flavor CLI packaging model from install/README.md: 'lean' (built-in extensions only) vs 'full' (built-in + add-on extensions bundled), 6 supported RIDs (win/linux-x64/arm64, macos-arm64). Trace the agent's OWN packaging seam because it ships as a separate extension bundle: AgentInstallLayout (Agent/AgentInstallLayout.cs:22) defines AgentExtensionDir as Extensions/Microsoft.Azure.Azclips.Extensions.Agent/ (:32-33), with prompts/ and deps/runtimes/<rid>/native/ staged there for packaged builds versus dev-loop defaults (:35-45); the actual staging is performed by devops/scripts/packaging/stage_agent.ps1 and stage_agent.sh. Cover devops/scripts/packaging/{common,windows,linux,macos,powershell,signing,config}/ (build_common.sh, create_component_archives.sh, inject_builtin_extensions.ps1/.sh, rename_extension_packages.sh) and devops/scripts/publishing/Update-ReleaseChangelog.ps1. Cover the end-user install scripts install/azcli-install.ps1 / .sh (and their uninstall counterparts) which fetch GitHub-hosted release archives via `gh api ... | bash`, installing to `~/.local/share/azcli` (or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\azcli`) WITHOUT modifying PATH by default — deliberately coexisting with classic azure-cli. Diagram: source -> per-extension build (OutputPath by ExtName) -> stage_agent -> component archive -> signed release asset -> install script -> ~/.local/share/azcli.

children.title: Testing & Build Pipeline
children.prompt: Explain the test and build/CI strategy. Test projects (from azclips.slnx and tests/): Cli.Tests, Cmdlets.Tests, Common (Tests.Common shared helpers), Core.Engine.Tests (e.g. ExecutionSessionSeamTests.cs — testing the ExecutionSession seam described in the Core Engine page), Core.Extensions.Tests, Core.Telemetry.Tests, Benchmark (BenchmarkDotNet), and Fixtures for assembly-loading/multi-version scenarios; plus Agent/tests/Core.Agent.Tests/ (ClosingToolPredicateTests.cs, ProposePlanValidationTests.cs, SubmitResponseValidationTests.cs, ExtractCommandNameTests.cs, ExtractPlanStepsTests.cs, EventRendererSnapshotTests.cs, ConsoleApprovalPromptTests.cs, PlanGateTests.cs, ArmCacheRefresherTests.cs, EnvironmentProberTests.cs, ShellOutHelperTests.cs — unit-testing the pure PlanArgsParser/PreToolUseHook logic in isolation from the live SDK, per Agent/tests/Core.Agent.Tests/AgentToolsLiveTests.cs for the live-SDK-dependent subset). Framework is xUnit with settings centralized in tests/Directory.Build.props and Agent/tests/Directory.Build.props. Cover build/build.ps1 and build/Install-BuildDependencies.ps1 (PlatyPS for help artifacts) and build/New-PSHelpMarkdown.ps1 / Set-ModuleConfiguration.ps1. Cover CI: devops/scripts/ci/check_pull_request.py, and the packaging pipeline consuming build output (link to Packaging & Distribution). Cover tools/Help (the help-generation tool backing `az agent tool help` and the CLI's own --help). Cover the openspec/ workflow (openspec/changes/profile-management/ as a worked example of proposal/design/tasks/specs) as the repository's design-doc process referenced by AGENTS.md. Diagram: source -> `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` -> coverage -> CI gate (check_pull_request.py) -> packaging.
